title: weighted-queue-and-kv-pin-timeouts-to-mitigate-starvation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Improves continuous-batcher fairness and prevents long-tail starvation by introducing a weighted queue throttler and KV-cache pin expiry tuning. No API changes; rollout controlled by feature flag.
description: Context: Production traces and perf canaries exposed recurring tail-latency regressions under mixed workloads with hot and cold tenants. Root cause analysis showed that the continuous batching scheduler's FIFO-dominant queue allowed small high-priority requests to be repeatedly overtaken when the runtime favored large batched prefixes; simultaneously the KV cache had a long pin expiry that amplified hot-key monopolization. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) a lightweight weighted-queue throttler in the continuous batcher that enforces service-share weights at queue admission time (soft scheduling), and 2) adjustable KV-cache pin timeouts and a small-metadata eviction hint to reduce long-running pin monopolies. Design: - Admissions now record a per-queue weight token and a sliding-window deficit counter; long-running peers lose admission weight over configurable windows to prevent starvation. - The scheduler still batches by model/seq-length compatibility, but before combining candidates we apply a fast O(1) fairness filter that reorders a small prefix of the queue based on deficit and age. This preserves batching efficiency for the common case while bounding unfairness. - KV cache: introduce per-tenant pin_ttl (default lowered from 30s -> 8s) and a 'soft-evict' hint that allows cold-key compaction during sustained high memory pressure. - Feature gate: both features are behind runtime flags (batcher.weighted_queue=true, kv.pin_adaptive=true) and can be tuned via config map in Dedicated/Private. Implementation notes: - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.rs: added WeightedQueue struct, deficit accounting, admission helpers, unit tests for corner cases. - runtime/scheduler/queue.rs: added peek-and-reorder primitive with micro-optimizations to avoid allocations. - runtime/kv_cache/pinning.rs: introduced pin_ttl, soft_evict hints, metrics for pin_count and pin_ttl_hist. - tests/scheduler_integration.rs: new deterministic multi-tenant load harness and long-tail assertion checks. - docs/ops/continuous-batcher-tuning.md: operator-facing notes and suggested knob values for common workloads. Performance summary: - Canary synthetic workload (10 tenants; mix heavy/light): P95 request latency reduced by 22% for light tenants and P99 reduced by 14% overall when feature gate enabled; end-to-end throughput unchanged within 3%. - Microbench: weighted admission adds ~150ns median overhead per admission check; observed <1% CPU cost at 100k qps. Testing and rollout: - Unit tests added for deficit accounting, corner cases for zero-weight tenants, and KV pin expiry behaviour. - Integration canary run in staging for 48h before merge. - Rollout plan: enable behind feature gate for 10% of Dedicated clusters, observe tail metrics for 72h, then ramp to 100% with monitor playbook. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve existing behavior (feature gates off). Related work: builds on ENG-7120 (continuous-batcher refactor) and pairs with upcoming kernel-level scheduling hints (ENG-8350).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez (2026-02-19): Comment: The deficit window constant seems conservative; did you try a 2s window instead of 5s? Also please add unit tests for zero-weight tenants.

Maya Chen (2026-02-19): Reply: I tried 2s in the microbench but saw slightly more reordering churn causing marginal batch inefficiency; 5s is a good middle ground but made configurable. I added tests for zero-weight tenants (see tests commit).
Priya Natarajan (2026-02-20): Comment: KV pin ttl default reduction looks large. Any regression risk for hot-key throughput? Please include metrics and an optional override per-tenant.
Maya Chen (2026-02-20): Reply: We included per-tenant override; microbench shows hot-key throughput <2% change at 8s default. Added metrics pin_ttl_hist and pin_count for monitoring (prometheus).
Liam O'Reilly (2026-02-21): Request changes: please add a long-running canary result snippet for mixed seq-length workloads and document the feature flags in the helm chart values.yaml.
Maya Chen (2026-02-22): Update: added canary dashboard screenshots and values.yaml example in docs. Re-ran integration canary for 48h; appended results to PR description.
Diego Alvarez (2026-02-23): Approval: LGTM after nits addressed. Priya approved after verifying canary graphs. Merging once CI passes.

merge_commit_message: squash: weighted queue & kv-pin: mitigate batcher starvation (#31247)
rollout_notes: Feature gated. Default off. Suggested default knobs: batcher.weighted_queue.window=5000ms, batcher.weighted_queue.prefix_size=8, kv.pin_ttl.default=8000ms. Start with 10% Dedicated, monitor P95/P99 per-tenant for 72h.
